🚨 **BLOCKING: engine-written labels can exceed the 96/20 marker-predicate budget — the engine's own markers stop resolving as markers**

`toolHistogramLabel` (`ledger_budget.dart:247`) caps the histogram at 3 *entries* but not at *characters*: with long tool names (MCP-style — this repo's own `mcp__flutter_agent_harness__codegraph_callers`-family names) the label is 174 chars, and both persisted shapes exceed the marker predicate:

```
label (174 chars): mcp__flutter_agent_harness__codegraph_callers ×1 · mcp__…__codegraph_impact_analysis ×1 · mcp__…__session_search_tool ×1 · 12:41–13:44
consolidatedHideMarker(...)  (191 chars) → isCompactionMarkerText = false
collapsedLedgerMarkerText(...) (212 chars) → isCompactionMarkerText = false
ledgerMarkerRef(...) → null
```

The change's own invariant (`markers.dart:175-182`) says the grown budget "covers every ENGINE shape" — that holds only if labels stay ≤96 chars/≤20 words, and nothing enforces it. Consequences when a batch's top-3 tool names are long:

- **The ledger budget silently under-counts**: `ledgerMarkerRef` returns null for the marker, so these C5 consolidated markers escape the 1000-token render cap entirely — the ≈18k runaway C4 exists to prevent can re-enter through the labels C5 adds.
- **Renumbering boundaries are missed**: `isPinRenumberingBoundary` gates the operative-pin carrier placement (`operative_pins.dart:524`, gh-1409 E6) and the image-citation re-basing (`image_registry.dart:753`, issue #195 F2). A boundary the predicate rejects lets a pin block render inside the summarized range and stale `[Image N]` citations rebind to the wrong image.
- Tool-pairing repair's cut boundary is missed too (`tool_pairing.dart:702`), so orphan notes mislabel the cut.

Note the doc comment's other half stays true: *model-written* labels pass `sanitizeHideLabel` (48/6) and always fit. It is the new **engine** histograms that are uncapped.

**Fix**: cap the label at build time in `toolHistogramLabel`/`hideBatchLabels` — drop histogram entries (then the span) until the head fits the predicate budget. Export the budget constants (`_markerLabelMaxChars`/`_markerLabelMaxWords`) as shared `hideLabelMax*`-style constants so the builder and the predicate cannot drift (the repo's one-source-of-truth discipline). Add a UT with three long MCP names pinning `isCompactionMarkerText(collapsedLedgerMarkerText(...))` and the persisted `consolidatedHideMarker(...)` is `true`.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `ledgerMarkerRef` misparses a per-record hidden marker whose preview quotes an `[expand a-b]` pointer**

The expand-pointer regex (`ledger_budget.dart:101`) is `firstMatch` anywhere in the marker text and is tried BEFORE the per-record branch — but a per-record marker carries a bounded content preview of the record's raw first line (`markerPreview`, 80 chars, not sanitized against pointers), and this codebase's own docs state that genuine content quotes pointers (`markers.dart:181-184`: "docs and skill texts quote `[expand 3-140]`").
```
marker text : [142:hidden·user·1.2k·"see the fold quoted as [expand 3-140] above"]
ledgerMarkerRef -> first=3 last=140 hiddenCount=138 mergeable=true
```

A marker that actually names hidden seq **142** is planned as covering **3–140**. When the budget pass merges it, `collapsedLedgerMarkerText` emits a door for the wrong span: expanding it hits records that were never hidden here (the honest "visible, nothing to expand" replies, or worse a checkpoint-covered range), while seq 142 — the record the marker stood for — loses its address in the request. The marker count ("N records hidden") is also computed from the bogus span.

Reaches production whenever a hidden user/assistant/orphaned-result first line contains a full `[expand N-M]` literal and the request is over the ledger budget (long compacted sessions — exactly this repo's working regime). Raising to 🚨 is warranted if you find the misparse reachable without the over-budget precondition.

**Fix**: test the per-record `[\d+:hidden·` prefix first and only fall through to the expand branch when the text has no per-record prefix (a consolidated/fold marker never starts with one); or end-anchor the expand match with a clean one-line, bracket-free head, mirroring `_isEngineExpandPointer`'s discipline. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the collapse merges markers that are NOT adjacent in the rendered request — the documented "no visible record between" invariant is not enforced**

`planLedgerBudget` picks "the first two spans that sit next to each other" by scanning the refs list only (`ledger_budget.dart:166`), and `_applyHiddenLedgerBudget` collects refs from ALL emissions. But between two mergeable markers a request can carry a checkpoint marker (excluded from refs by the `·ckpt·` check), a dropped-fold note, or simply a visible record. The docstring promises "their original positions are consecutive among the SURVIVING markers — no visible record between", and `docs/compaction.md` (C4 section) promises "every id a collapsed pointer names is still hidden in the session file — the door resolves". Neither holds. Verified with the production `collapseLedgerMarkers` (same `planLedgerBudget` core), budget 10:

```
in:  [5:hidden] · "a visible user record sits here (never hidden)" · [7:hidden] · [9:ckpt·…·covers:9,10] · [12:hidden]
out: "3 records hidden [expand 5-12]" · "a visible user record…" · "[9:ckpt·…]"
```

The merged door `[expand 5-12]` spans the visible record and the checkpoint-covered range. Expanding it re-materializes the checkpoint's whole covered range alongside the checkpoint text (the count line says 3 — the model is told it is opening 3 records and gets 21+), and the visible record answers "visible, nothing to expand". Both docs claims above are false for exactly the sessions C4 targets (multi-escalation + heavy hide loads).

**Fix**: make adjacency real — in `_applyHiddenLedgerBudget`, split the refs into contiguous emission runs (`ref[i+1].index == ref[i].index + 1`) and plan each run separately (a run of one is never merged). Cheap, local, and restores both the docstring and the docs claim. Add a UT with a visible record / checkpoint between two over-budget marker runs.

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: pin-flush failure loses already-resolved ids — and the docstring's retry promise is false**

`_flushChildSteeringPins` calls `takeForFlush()` BEFORE the appends. Inside `takeForFlush` the resolved lists are reset and `pinnedSteeringRecordIds` is already advanced to the new delivery. If the `appendSegmentPin` then throws (disk full, storage hiccup — exactly when the record WAS persisted but the pin did not land), the resolved record ids are consumed and gone: the steering record never pins, silently — the precise worker-A failure mode C2 exists to prevent. The next delivery's flush then also emits a bogus release for ids that were never pinned in the file.

The docstring (`task_executor.dart:2515-2517`) claims the opposite: "a failed pin append leaves the pins pending (the next flush retries; the session is untouched)" — that retry does not exist for this path.

Suggest commit-on-success: copy the resolved lists, run the appends, and only reset the lists / advance `pinnedSteeringRecordIds` after both appends succeed; on failure leave everything pending so the next flush genuinely retries (and then the docstring becomes true). Bounded impact today (best-effort contract), but the code should either honor its stated contract or state the real one.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: C2 (pinned steering) and C7 (prompt include) are solid — well-tested at unit and IT level, REG-6 respected. The C4/C5 ledger work has one blocking gap: the new engine-generated histogram labels are uncapped, so with long (MCP-style) tool names the engine's own persisted markers fail `isCompactionMarkerText`, escape the ledger budget accounting, and break the pin/image renumbering boundary invariants — plus two confirmed C4 robustness bugs that produce wrong `[expand]` doors.

**Next Steps**:
1. 🚨 Cap `toolHistogramLabel` at the marker-predicate budget (96/20) at build time; share the budget constants; UT with three long MCP names (comment 1, repro included)
2. ⚠️ Fix `ledgerMarkerRef` pointer misparse — per-record prefix check before the expand branch (comment 2, repro included)
3. ⚠️ Enforce true emission-adjacency when planning merges — split refs into contiguous runs (comment 3, repro included)

If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a2245d-9fd8-71b3-b9ba-93e1e37bb362/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

## The owner talks to you only

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout. A `cmd &`/nohup survivor of a call is adopted as a tracked job (completion reported; no captured output or exit code).

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true, and adopted cmd & / nohup survivors). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: working_set
tools.description: Save your working set: the short status (decisions made, never-do list, next steps, rules to keep) pinned into the system prompt of every request. It survives compaction and resume; the newest replaces the previous one; "" clears it. Max 4096 chars — longer text is refused, not clipped.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

tools.name: others
tools.description: Deferred tools (not loaded): agent_directory, agent_message, ask, checkpoint, compact_expand, config, memory_delete, memory_list, request_secret, rewind, schedule_message, task, task_cancel, task_observe, task_resume, task_send, task_status. Call others with tool_name to load a tool's full description and schema; omit tool_name to list them with one-line docs.

content.text:
Senior Code Reviewer ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input//` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input//`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## input_context.md # PR Review Input Context — reading order (base contract) Reviewer-agnostic: EVERY reviewer leg reads the same PR context. Read files that exist in `input/` locally — do NOT re-fetch via dmtools. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_findings.md — previously raised findings (when present)"] P8["8️⃣ input/TICKET/review_policy.md — the resolved reviewPolicy: severity table, density cap, downgrade protocol"] P9["9️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_new_hunks.txt — the hunks added since the last reviewed head (re-review rounds; when present)"] P10["🔟 input/TICKET/pool_specialist-.md — THIS session's pool-specialist prompt (specialist sessions only; when present)"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 --> P8 --> P9 --> P10 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## Pool specialist sessions — the pool prompt file When the run's prompt file is `input/TICKET/pool_specialist-.md`, this session is ONE reviewer's focused pass of the reviewer pool — not the posting review. The prompt names the reviewer, its lens, the output contract and the round head. A specialist session: - hunts ONLY its lens's dimension (the lens file it is pointed at names it) — the generalist posting pass owns everything else; - writes `outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json` per the base candidates-only contract (output_rules.md) — NEVER `outputs/pr_review.json`, never `pr_review_general.md`, never `pr_review_comments/*`; - posts nothing, labels nothing, changes no status — the aggregation step reads the candidates file and the posting session stamps the markers. A session WITHOUT a pool-specialist prompt is the posting review: the full verdict contract below applies unchanged. ## output_rules.md # PR Review Output Rules — the machine contract (base) Reviewer-agnostic: every reviewer leg writes the same structured review artifacts; the machine parses them. The lens may add reviewer-specific files but never changes this contract. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for the PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ## The contract - `outputs/pr_review.json` — valid JSON with `recommendation` (APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | BLOCK), `summary`, `generalComment`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts`. - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — the general PR comment body; max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays. - `outputs/pr_review_comments/.md` — one file per detailed inline comment; the `comment` field carries the file PATH, never the text itself. - Each inline comment: `path`, `line`, `startLine`, `side`, `comment`, `severity` (BLOCKING | IMPORTANT | SUGGESTION | NIT). - Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff (use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks; if `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the exact line). A finding on unchanged code outside the diff goes to `pr_review_general.md` — never an inline thread. - If `ci_failures.md` is present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in `ci_failures_full.log`). - Keep `summary` under 2 sentences — details live in the inline comment files, not the general text. - Ticket context: verify the PR changes satisfy the ticket ACs — note gaps in the review. - The verdict is a MACHINE decision recomputed from `issueCounts` + the resolved `reviewPolicy` — the census is the machine's source of truth; keep it accurate. ## The candidates-only contract (pool specialist sessions) A pool specialist session (its prompt file is `input/TICKET/pool_specialist-.md` — see input_context.md) writes ONE file and nothing else: `outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json` ```json { "reviewer": "", "head": "", "candidates": [ {"id": 1, "path": "src/auth/UserService.js", "line": 45, "severity": "BLOCKING", "claim": "one-paragraph statement of the finding"}, {"id": 2, "path": "docs/arch.md", "line": null, "severity": "SUGGESTION", "claim": "a digest candidate — no diff line"} ], "count": 2, "truncated": false, "at": "" } ``` - `claim` is the finding's substance: what is wrong, where the evidence is, why it matters. No severity header line, no verdict language — the tier rides the `severity` field (BLOCKING | IMPORTANT | SUGGESTION | NIT) and the machine classifies the posted thread from it. - `id` numbers the candidates within the file (1..n). `path` is repo-relative; `line` is the diff line (right-hand side) or `null` for a digest candidate — findings anchored outside the diff are allowed as digest candidates, never as invented line numbers. - Write NOTHING else: no `outputs/pr_review.json`, no `pr_review_general.md`, no `pr_review_comments/*`, no `response.md`. Do not post, label, resolve threads, or change statuses — the aggregation step reads this file and the posting review does all machine bookkeeping (the merged census + the marker stamps). - Severity discipline still applies: raise only what the lens hunt justifies; an empty candidates list is a valid answer (the leg completes with zero findings). - The candidates pass the finding filter like every other finding (fresh verification, weighted retention for high-weight reviewers) and the posting leg merges them into ONE review — a specialist never posts a second review. ### The coverage file (the second specialist output — the memory) Alongside the candidates file the specialist maintains ONE more file: `outputs/pr_review_coverage-.json` ```json { "reviewer": "", "head": "", "covered": ["src/auth/UserService.js"], "pending": ["docs/arch.md", "src/auth/Session.js"], "truncated": false, "at": "" } ``` - **Write it FIRST** — before any review: `covered: []`, `pending:` the full list of repo files you plan to review (your pass's scope). - Move files `pending` → `covered` as you finish them (re-write the file). The file is re-read by the machine after your session ends, whatever its cause — a timeout kills the session but not what landed on disk. - The NEXT pass receives this file as memory: covered files that the fresh hunks do not touch are skipped (unchanged — machine-verified), still- pending files are finished first. Big requests converge: every round reviews the delta plus the oldest debt, until nothing is pending. - `truncated: true` near the cap: unfinished files stay `pending` — a partial honest record is a valid state, silence is not. ## registry_protocol.md # Finding-identity registry protocol (base contract) Reviewer-agnostic: every reviewer leg answers the same previously-raised findings registry before raising anything new. This protocol is a factory invariant — the machine parses the dispositions. ## 9. Previously raised findings — the finding-identity registry When `input/TICKET/pr_findings.md` is present, earlier review rounds on this PR already raised findings **F1–Fn** (each with its claim, file and status). The registry dedup is what keeps repeated rounds from minting duplicate threads for the same defect. Answer the registry **before** raising anything new: - **verify fixed** — the fixing hunk you can cite closes the finding: disposition `"fixed"` with the hunk reference. Never mark `fixed` without a citable hunk. - **withdraw (reason required)** — the claim is wrong or no longer applies: disposition `"withdrawn"` with the reason. A withdrawal without a reason is rejected by the machine, and BLOCKING withdrawals surface to the owner. - **mark re-introduced** — the defect is still there (e.g. the fix was reverted): leave the finding open and let your re-raise match it; do not re-litigate the claim from scratch. New claims always need new evidence, and they pass the same §7 necessity test before they earn a thread. A finding on the registry list is answered, not re-raised as if it were news. **Candidates pending confirmation** (also listed in `pr_findings.md`): when a new finding you raised is *possibly same as F*, the machine asks one word per candidate — confirm with `"same as F"` or call it `"new"`. Unconfirmed candidates become new identities; nothing merges without your confirmation. This is a dedup request, not a push-back: confirming merges the threads, it does not weaken the finding (merges can only escalate severity, never de-escalate). Add a `findingReview` block to `outputs/pr_review.json` (alongside `inlineComments`): ```json {"findingReview": { "dispositions": [ {"n": 1, "status": "fixed", "hunk": "src/auth.ts:40-48 — try/catch added"}, {"n": 2, "status": "withdrawn", "reason": "validation exists at src/auth.ts:50 — claim was wrong"}, {"n": 3, "status": "re-introduced"} ], "confirmations": [ {"proposedFor": 1, "same": true} ] }} ``` When `pr_findings.md` is absent, this section does not apply — review exactly as before. ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION|NIT)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional clarity · NIT = style only"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` ## few_shots_format.md # pr_review.json shape — format contract (base) Reviewer-agnostic: the structured answer of every reviewer leg carries the same shape. The worked examples live in each reviewer's few-shots file; this file is the shape + severity-boundary contract. ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":20,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","severity":"NIT"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1,"nits":1} } ``` **Severity boundary (4 tiers)**: a 🪶 NIT changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented (style, naming, formatting, micro-symmetry); a 💡 SUGGESTION changes clarity of the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Anything that changes behavior or breaks a documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING. The 4-tier census (`issueCounts`) counts posted threads + digest lines and drives the machine verdict — keep it consistent with the inlineComments severities. ### outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json — pool specialist sessions only A pool specialist session (its prompt file present) answers with candidates, never a verdict — the posting review mints the verdict; the aggregation merges, the filter verifies and the posting review posts. The record schema adds the head binding: ```json { "reviewer": "security", "head": "", "count": 2, "truncated": false, "at": "", "candidates": [ {"id": 1, "path": "src/auth/UserService.js", "line": 45, "severity": "BLOCKING", "claim": "User query at line 45 concatenates req.body.user straight into the SQL string; parameterize the statement."}, {"id": 2, "path": "docs/migration.md", "line": null, "severity": "SUGGESTION", "claim": "The rollback path for the new columns is undocumented — a bad deploy cannot revert cleanly."} ] } ``` Rules: `head` = the round head sha from the prompt (a stale file never feeds a newer head); `id` = position in the file; `path` repo-relative; `line` = the diff line or `null` for a digest candidate; `claim` = the substance (no severity header, no verdict language). Severity boundary identical to the verdict tiers above. Nothing else gets written (no pr_review.json, no comment files) and nothing gets posted — worked examples of the claim voice live in each reviewer's few-shots file. ## lens.md # Generalist Review Lens (the base reviewer) The generalist lens: full-diff review across every dimension. The reviewer-agnostic contract (input reading order, output rules, verdict rules, registry protocol, formatting) lives in `instructions/pr_review/base/` and is assembled around this lens — this file is WHAT the base reviewer hunts, not how it answers. ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Deep read:
first round — every changed file;
re-review (pr_new_hunks.txt present) —
new hunks + interaction neighborhood
(unchanged lines frozen)"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION / NIT
(severity census gates approval per review_policy.md)"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Necessity pass:
threads only for findings that defend

everything else → ranked digest"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: does each candidate finding pass the §7 necessity test (defends correctness on a touched path, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract) — or is it digest material? ## 3. Changed-file deep read — and frozen already-reviewed code Do not review from the diff alone. **First review round** (no `pr_new_hunks.txt` in the input folder) — read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact **Re-review rounds** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` present — the hunks added since the last reviewed head) — read the full content of the files the new hunks touch plus their interaction neighborhood (direct callers/callees of changed symbols), not whole files. Already-reviewed lines are **frozen**: a finding on an unchanged line is valid only when the new hunks make the problem worse (the interaction test — e.g. a new call path now feeds unvalidated input into old code). Anything else on frozen lines is advisory digest at most (§7), never a thread. If `pr_new_hunks.txt` is absent from a later round (e.g. a force-push the machine could not diff), the whole diff is in scope again. ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ### Delegate to the measured gates Complexity, duplication and style are already measured by the repo's CI — the CRAP ratchet, the duplication gate, lint. The gate is the reviewer of record for those dimensions: a passing gate is not a thread (the cost was already measured and accepted); a failing gate is CI breakage (🚨 BLOCKING). Raise a complexity/duplication/style finding only when no gate covers it **and** the concrete cost is stateable — what breaks or what the next change pays. ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement to the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Does not block merge. - **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Never blocks merge, never triggers a lap. When in doubt, classify lower and state what evidence would raise the finding one level (the same discipline as the external-spec citation rule below — an unproven claim must not hold a PR hostage). ### Density control — post top-K, digest the overflow `review_policy.md` in the input folder carries the resolved policy and its density cap (`allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8)` — 20→3 · 50→4 · 200→5 · 800→8): - The cap applies to 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT threads only — 🚨/⚠️ findings are **never capped** and always post as threads. - Rank your 💡/🪶 findings by value and post only the top-K as inline threads. - The overflow becomes a **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`). - The census counts posted threads + digest lines (`issueCounts.suggestions`/`nits` count posts, `digest` counts the overflow lines). - The machine audits the posted thread count against the cap (warn only — it never fails the leg). ### Downgrade protocol — honor a justified ⚠️→💡 from rework A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification in the census** (its thread reply and response summary). When the justification is present, classify the finding 💡 in this round's census — a false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. A silent downgrade does not exist: without the written justification, keep ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - **Before emitting a spec-claim finding without a citation, locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it (for example `ticket.md:12`) — an uncited true claim is demoted mechanically.** - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. The machine applies the same discipline (and a safety net against coin-flip formatting): every uncited spec claim is cross-checked against the ticket text the run already has under `input/`. When the requirement is verifiably present there, the finding keeps 🚨 BLOCKING force and the matched citation is auto-appended; when the ticket contradicts it, lacks it, or the mechanical check is inconclusive, the finding is demoted and stamped `demoted-from-BLOCKING` — the finding-identity registry keeps it re-elevatable in a later round by adding a citation instead of raising the same defect as new. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Necessity test — what earns a thread A thread is expensive: each one costs a rework lap — 15–20 CI minutes — and the rework's own fresh hunks get reviewed again next round. A finding earns a thread only if it **defends** one of: - correctness on a path the change actually touches - security - data loss - CI breakage - the ticket contract Everything else — real, accurate, but not merge-relevant — goes to the **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`), never a thread. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists — classify everything you found; only the necessity test decides thread vs digest. - The exhaustive pass keeps running (§3 defines its scope). Re-read the in-scope code and ask: *"What else does this change put at risk?"* — not *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify each thread you are about to open passes the necessity test; everything else is already in the digest. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## few_shots.md Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":20,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","severity":"NIT"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1,"nits":1} } ``` **Severity boundary (4 tiers)**: a 🪶 NIT changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented (style, naming, formatting, micro-symmetry); a 💡 SUGGESTION changes clarity of the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Anything that changes behavior or breaks a documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING. ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## review_verdict_rules.md # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings into 4 tiers: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — clarity of the documented/behavioral surface: missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape. - 🪶 **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Then map to the verdict (the machine recomputes it from the census — `postPRReviewComments` treats your token as advisory): | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | Any ⚠️ IMPORTANT (no 🚨) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` (gates approval — policy default) | | Only 💡 / 🪶 remain | `APPROVE` — the cycle converges | **Downgrade protocol:** when the rework lap downgraded a specific ⚠️ to 💡 **with a written justification in the census** (the thread reply states why the finding is not maintainability debt), classify that finding 💡 in this round's census — the false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. Without the written justification, keep ⚠️: a silent downgrade does not exist, and the machine recomputes the verdict from the census you post. `APPROVE` with remaining 💡/🪶 findings is the expected terminal state (the resolved policy's `allowApproveWithSuggestions` derives from the tier table — SUGGESTION rounds polish, NIT rounds none): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID

dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ## bash_tools.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SHELLSTATE["⚠️ Persistent-shell pitfalls (sandbox-observed)"] P1["Never end commands with exit — it kills the shell session, making read_bash fail with Invalid shell ID"] P2["Capture the exit code via $? right after the command, before running anything else — a late $? reads the wrong command's code"] P3["Avoid $PIPESTATUS — it produced wrong exit codes in the sandbox; redirect output to a file and check $? instead"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). - **PR #**: 2499
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2499
- **Title**: gh-2492 GOAL #29 (remainder): compaction C2 pinned steering for task children + C4 ledger_budget split-out + C5 hide-only summary + C6 one-window check + C7 prompt rules (split from #2423)

## PR Description

Closes #2492
### What changed

GOAL #29 remainder (C2/C4/C5/C6/C7) — the compaction changes live on branch
`ai/gh-2492` as one commit per component (C1/C3 already landed via #2423):

- **C2 — pinned steering for task children** (`6799324`): a task child's task
  prompt record and newest steering delivery pin in its OWN session file
  (`SegmentPinRecord`): the prompt pins once on its first flush; every
  steering delivery pins its records and releases the previous delivery's; a
  resume from a pre-card session gains ensure-pins (never un-hiding). The
  mechanical trim valve (`localTrimValve`) carries pinned messages behind its
  cut. Mail stays data — `isSyntheticUserText` untouched (REG-6).
- **C4+C5 — the hidden-ledger budget + consolidated hide labels**
  (`8608576`): the four bare hide writers (judge hide, deterministic
  fallback, LRU re-hide, EmergencyRelief) consolidate each batch into ONE
  `hidden_range` record with an engine-generated histogram label (tool
  events + time span, no model text), rendered as
  `<label> [expand a-b]`. A render-time budget (`hiddenLedgerBudgetTokens`
  = 1000 over all hidden markers of a request) collapses the oldest adjacent
  markers into working `N records hidden · <label> [expand a-b]` pointers
  until the ledger fits — no file rewrite, deterministic across rebuilds,
  the expandable set never changes.
- **C6 — one-window consistency** (`59475b1`): a REG test pins that trigger,
  over-window guard, both notices and the ctx meter resolve the SAME window
  for catalog-only, registry-pinned (endpoint report, user pin, shrink) and
  owner-capped identities. No production change was needed.
- **C7 — the pinned-steering include** (`ae690a9`):
  `prompts/compaction/pinned_steering.md` rides the mode prompt and every
  task child's system prompt beside the working-set and context-hygiene
  includes (child fixture calibration grows by the measured footprint).
- **Docs + changelog** (`f5a8e93`): `docs/compaction.md` sections per
  component; `changelog/entries/2492-*.md` (CHANGELOG.md stays a generated
  index).

### Key decisions

- Pin bookkeeping lives in the executor's transcript flush (the session's
  single writer) keyed on message-object identity — robust against notice
  interleaving and the post-compaction flush-cursor reset (#387).
- The ledger budget is enforced at RENDER time only (per #2423 §C4: no file
  rewrite); labels derive from the covered records, so a rebuild yields the
  identical view.
- The engine-marker predicate's label budget grows to the engine's own
  shapes (96 chars / 16 words); model-written labels stay at the tight
  sanitizer budget (48/6) — UT-26's negative case updated to sit beyond it.
- One commit per component on one branch (the pipeline opens one PR).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/task/subagent_steering_pins_test.dart   # C2: pins (6)
dart test test/compaction/trim_valve_pins_test.dart    # C2 belt: valve (3)
dart test test/compaction/ledger_budget_test.dart      # C4 unit (12)
dart test test/compaction/ledger_budget_projection_test.dart  # C4 wired (3)
dart test test/compaction/hide_batch_labels_test.dart  # C5 writers (3)
dart test test/compaction/one_window_test.dart         # C6 REG (5)
dart test test/prompts/                                # C7 sync (53)
dart analyze lib/ test/                                # clean
```

Full suite: `dart test test/` — 2459+ green on the component suites; the
final full run is recorded on the branch.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[parent task_send / resume] --> TE[task_executor]
  TE -->|prompt + steering objects| FL[transcript flush - single writer]
  FL -->|SegmentPinRecord| SF[child session file]
  SF --> W[valve localTrimValve pinnedMessages]
  SF --> PRJ[projection: render]

```

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-28):

🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: engine-written labels can exceed the 96/20 marker-predicate budget — the engine's own markers stop resolving as markers**

`toolHistogramLabel` (`ledger_budget.dart:247`) caps the histogram at 3 *entries* but not at *characters*: with long tool names (MCP-style — this repo's own `mcp__flutter_agent_harness__codegraph_callers`-family names) the label is 174 chars, and both persisted shapes exceed the marker predicate:

```
label (174 chars): mcp__flutter_agent_harness__codegraph_callers ×1 · mcp__…__codegraph_impact_analysis ×1 · mcp__…__session_search_tool ×1 · 12:41–13:44
consolidatedHideMarker(...)  (191 chars) → isCompactionMarkerText = false
collapsedLedgerMarkerText(...) (212 chars) → isCompactionMarkerText = false
ledgerMarkerRef(...) → null
```

The change's own invariant (`markers.dart:175-182`) says the grown budget "covers every ENGINE shape" — that holds only if labels stay ≤96 chars/≤20 words, and nothing enforces it. Consequences when a batch's top-3 tool names are long:

- **The ledger budget silently under-counts**: `ledgerMarkerRef` returns null for the marker, so these C5 consolidated markers escape the 1000-token render cap entirely — the ≈18k runaway C4 exists to prevent can re-enter through the labels C5 adds.
- **Renumbering boundaries are missed**: `isPinRenumberingBoundary` gates the operative-pin carrier placement (`operative_pins.dart:524`, gh-1409 E6) and the image-citation re-basing (`image_registry.dart:753`, issue #195 F2). A boundary the predicate rejects lets a pin block render inside the summarized range and stale `[Image N]` citations rebind to the wrong image.
- Tool-pairing repair's cut boundary is missed too (`tool_pairing.dart:702`), so orphan notes mislabel the cut.

Note the doc comment's other half stays true: *model-written* labels pass `sanitizeHideLabel` (48/6) and always fit. It is the new **engine** histograms that are uncapped.

**Fix**: cap the label at build time in `toolHistogramLabel`/`hideBatchLabels` — drop histogram entries (then the span) until the head fits the predicate budget. Export the budget constants (`_markerLabelMaxChars`/`_markerLabelMaxWords`) as shared `hideLabelMax*`-style constants so the builder and the predicate cannot drift (the repo's one-source-of-truth discipline). Add a UT with three long MCP names pinning `isCompactionMarkerText(collapsedLedgerMarkerText(...))` and the persisted `consolidatedHideMarker(...)` is `true`.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-28):

⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `ledgerMarkerRef` misparses a per-record hidden marker whose preview quotes an `[expand a-b]` pointer**

The expand-pointer regex (`ledger_budget.dart:101`) is `firstMatch` anywhere in the marker text and is tried BEFORE the per-record branch — but a per-record marker carries a bounded content preview of the record's raw first line (`markerPreview`, 80 chars, not sanitized against pointers), and this codebase's own docs state that genuine content quotes pointers (`markers.dart:181-184`: "docs and skill texts quote `[expand 3-140]`"). Verified against the production code:

```
marker text : [142:hidden·user·1.2k·"see the fold quoted as [expand 3-140] above"]
ledgerMarkerRef -> first=3 last=140 hiddenCount=138 mergeable=true
```

A marker that actually names hidden seq **142** is planned as covering **3–140**. When the budget pass merges it, `collapsedLedgerMarkerText` emits a door for the wrong span: expanding it hits records that were never hidden here (the honest "visible, nothing to expand" replies, or worse a checkpoint-covered range), while seq 142 — the record the marker stood for — loses its address in the request. The marker count ("N records hidden") is also computed from the bogus span.

Reaches production whenever a hidden user/assistant/orphaned-result first line contains a full `[expand N-M]` literal and the request is over the ledger budget (long compacted sessions — exactly this repo's working regime). Raising to 🚨 is warranted if you find the misparse reachable without the over-budget precondition.

**Fix**: test the per-record `[\d+:hidden·` prefix first and only fall through to the expand branch when the text has no per-record prefix (a consolidated/fold marker never starts with one); or end-anchor the expand match with a clean one-line, bracket-free head, mirroring `_isEngineExpandPointer`'s discipline. Add a UT with a preview-quoted pointer.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the collapsed count-line reserve is hardcoded to 3-digit counts — at the cap's own maximum a ≥1000-record merged pointer stops resolving as a marker**

The new reserve (`ledger_budget.dart:321`) assumes `'999 records hidden · '` (21 chars) is "the worst case the count can add" — provably false: a 4-digit count adds 22 chars, a 5-digit one 23. `_capEngineLabel` therefore allows labels up to 75 chars, and `collapsedLedgerMarkerText` renders the head without re-checking. Verified at the exact boundary (production code):

```
label=75 chars (the cap's own max) · countLine for 999  = 21 → head 96 → predicate=true,  budgetRef=3
label=75 chars · countLine for 1000 = 22 → head 97 → predicate=false, budgetRef=null
label=75 chars · countLine for 10000 = 23 → head 98 → predicate=false, budgetRef=null
```

`isCompactionMarkerText=false` means the collapsed pointer escapes `ledgerMarkerRef` (its tokens never count toward the 1000-token budget — the exact under-count F1 fixed) and is missed as a renumbering boundary (`operative_pins.dart`, `image_registry.dart`, `tool_pairing.dart` — the gh-1409 E6 / #195 F2 failure modes). It also contradicts the two claims this rework added: the reserve docstring ("worst case the count can add") and the changelog/docs claim that "BOTH persisted shapes always resolve as markers".

Reachability: `hiddenCount` ≥ 1000 needs a chain-merge accumulating ~4 of the measured ~280-record consolidated batches (docs/compaction.md cites "five cycles × ~280 records") in ONE contiguous emission run, or the equivalent mixed per-record/consolidated chain — the tail of the exact long-run regime this subsystem targets. Raise to 🚨 if ≥1000-record chains are considered common in practice.

**Fix**: the count is known at merge time — clamp the label inside `collapsedLedgerMarkerText` against the full rendered head (`markerLabelMaxChars - '$hiddenCount records hidden · '.length`), dropping to the already-documented bare-pointer shape when nothing fits; then the reserve constants in `_capEngineLabel` only need to cover the cap-shape (`<label> [expand a-b]`), not the count shape. Update the reserve docstring and the docs wording. A UT at label=75 + count=1000 pins the boundary.

Round-2 review complete and all artifacts verified.

## Re-review verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES (PR #2499 round 2 — rework commit `5ee6379a8e`)

**Registry answered — all six round-1 findings verified FIXED** (each with a cited hunk + fresh repro against production code):

| id | disposition | evidence |
|----|-------------|----------|
| F1 label overflow | `fixed` | `_capEngineLabel` caps at build time; `markerLabelMaxChars/Words` now public shared constants; 174-char MCP label → 62 chars, both persisted shapes resolve, `ledgerMarkerRef` parses; UTs pin it |
| F2 pointer misparse | `fixed` | per-record branch now runs first; `[142:hidden·…"see [expand 3-140]"…]` parses 142/142/1; UTs cover it + consolidated still parses |
| F3 non-adjacent merges | `fixed` | contiguous emission runs (`index+1`); visible record + checkpoint between markers → 0 replacements; UTs |
| F4 bare print | `fixed` | print removed, silent catch, `runZoned` test asserts nothing prints |
| F5 pin-flush state loss | `fixed` | `takeForFlush` read-only + `commitFlush()` after success; release-integrity test (no release names an unpinned id) |
| F6 docs 16→20 words | `fixed` | docs + changelog now say 96/20 and name the shared constants |

**One new finding this round** — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the new count-line reserve is hardcoded to 3-digit counts (`'999 records hidden · '` = 21 chars, claimed as "the worst case"). Verified at the exact boundary: with a 75-char label (the cap's own maximum), a merged pointer with `hiddenCount ≥ 100` renders a 97+ char head → `isCompactionMarkerText=false`, `ledgerMarkerRef=null` — it escapes the 1000-token ledger budget and the pin/image renumbering boundaries again, contradicting the rework's own "BOTH persisted shapes always resolve" claim. Fix is local: clamp the label in `collapsedLedgerMarkerText` against the full rendered head (the count is known there).

**Verification**: 97 component/prompt tests pass, `dart analyze lib/ test/` clean, boundary repros run against the checked-out PR head. The merged-in main content (gh-2466 etc.) is already on `origin/main` and excluded from the PR diff — no review surface there. Census: blocking 0, important 1 → `REQUEST_CHANGES` per the policy table (an open ⚠️ gates approval).
